newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Weak won, economic woes dampen Korean gold demand.
newsitem.headline: Weak won, economic woes dampen Korean gold demand.

text.p: The won's sharp decline against the U.S. dollar has sent South Korean domestic gold prices higher, depressing demand already battered by the nation's economic woes, precious metal traders said on Tuesday.
The won fell to a new seven-year low early on Tuesday to 888.80 against the dollar on trade expectations of rising demand for the U.S. unit.

Demand for the dollar has been rising due to a growing trade deficit caused primarily by a downturn in South Korea's key export industries and the Japanese yen's steep depreciation against the dollar, local dealers said.
The customs-cleared trade deficit rose to US$23.72 billion in 1996 from a $10.06 billion shortfall in the previous year.

The collapse of Hanbo Steel in January and Sammi Steel last week, coupled with weeks of labour unrest in January which raised the possibility of further bankruptcies, further weakened demand for the yellow metal, dealers said.
Gold producer LG Metals' daily selling price for gold, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, rose on Tuesday to 10,400 won per gram from 10,250 won a week ago.
The company's silver price was steady at 164 won.
Traders said the financial failure of several local wholesalers also put a lid on domestic gold demand despite a squeeze on local supplies.
Two local bullion wholesalers, including Korea Diamond Co Ltd, recently defaulted on debt repayments of about 20 billion won, they said.
"(The) domestic precious metal industry is very sensitive to the domestic economy. It has reflected well where the economy goes," a bullion dealer said.
"Therefore, buyers, who used to buy 10 kilogram gold per month, now appear to buy five kilogram gold," the dealer said.
The dealer added the won's decline caused local bullion houses to reduce gold imports over fears of steep currency losses.
The telegraphic transfer selling rate for customers posted by the Korea Exchange Bank fell 7.50 won to 890.80 won against the dollar from 883.30 won a week ago.
The rate is regarded as a benchmark of local foreign exchange rates for companies here.
